Hi, nice to see you.

First, let's establish if this is your property, and if you're willing to make structural changes. If so, you could do it relatively cheaply, buying a mediocre hammock (or the material to make your own), and some basic hardware. If you can't make changes, you'll have to get a hammock stand, and that takes space, and will be costly for a decent ready-made one.

Secondly, have you slept in a hammock before, do you find it comfortable? I can sleep in the woods in a hammock, but not inside (mainly I think because the cheap frame I bought is shit), so try before you buy.

Pros: Cheaper than a bed. More space when stowed away. Easy to clean.

Cons: Must have somewhere secure to hang. Must be hung correctly. Can be cold in winter if your house has poor insulation. Can't (really) "sleep" two in a hammock...

Summary

/v/dreamworlds is a niche subverse dedicated to the feeling of something unusual, mysterious or unknown that occurs in an unfamiliar location.

History

Throughout my life, I've been pulled in by works of fiction set in a fantasy world. My earliest memorable experience with a fantasy world was when I got my first game system, the original Playstation, and the original Spyro game. Other examples of fantasy world games that have pulled me in are Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy, Kingdom Hearts, Oblivion, Metroid: Fusion, Runescape and World of Warcraft. Granted, some of these games aren't that old, but video gaming was my earliest memorable experience with fantasy worlds.

My next earliest experience with fantasy worlds was anime. I'm a pretty avid anime watcher. No, I'm not a weeaboo, but if I ever want to sit down and watch a show of some kind instead of playing video games, I watch anime. Here's my MyAnimeList (MAL) in case you're wondering. My first experiences with anime were way back when I was in Elementary School and still had a bedtime and my parents didn't want me watching TV past 9:00PM. Whenever I couldn't sleep, I'd go to Cartoonnetwork and they'd play anime late at night. Back then I didn't know it was called anime, I just thought it was a different flavor of cartoon. Because of the fact that I wasn't actively following these shows, I would be watching pieces of them from a point pretty far on in the plot, so I wouldn't have a damn clue what was going on. I loved that feeling that I got when I'd be watching a show and not having a damn clue what was going on, it would give me a mystified feeling, a sense of wonder. It would give me the impression that there's a big world out there to be explored.

My Message To You

I'm only one guy, but I'm slowly evolving my idea of what I want this subverse to be and what I want it to become. That being said, I'm always open to suggestions and feedback that anyone may have. This subverse is my own specific idea, so I'm going to be picky about what ideas get thrown at me, but I'm an open-minded person so if you have any suggestions or feedback I'd be happy to hear it.
